name: llmcord
test_cmd:
mkdir -p "$ENV/home" "$ENV/tmp" && HOME="$ENV/home" TMPDIR="$ENV/tmp" PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX="$ENV/tmp/pycache" OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-dummy DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN=dummy-token DISCORD_CLIENT_ID=0 $PY -c 'import asyncio, compileall, importlib, re, sys, time
t = time.time(); p = f = 0
if compileall.compile_dir(".", quiet=1, force=True, rx=re.compile(r"/[.]|node_modules")):
    p += 1
else:
    f += 1; print("FAILED compileall .")
asyncio.run = lambda coro, **kw: coro.close()
try:
    m = importlib.import_module("llmcord")
    assert callable(m.on_message) and callable(m.main) and m.config["models"]
    p += 1
except BaseException as e:
    f += 1; print("FAILED import llmcord:", repr(e))
dt = time.time() - t
print(f"{p} passed, {f} failed in {dt:.2f}s" if f else f"{p} passed in {dt:.2f}s")
sys.exit(1 if f else 0)'
notes: No test suite and no CI config (no tests/, no .github/; REPOS.json says tests: none), so test_cmd is a v3 smoke check. The repo is a single module, llmcord.py, at the root (not a package; nothing to install editable). Setup installs requirements.txt (discord.py>=2.6.0, httpx, openai, python-dotenv, pyyaml) into a uv venv; resolved discord-py 2.7.1, openai 3.29.0, httpx 0.28.1, python-dotenv 1.2.4, pyyaml 6.0.3. Python 3.12.15 (the Dockerfile uses python:3.13-slim; 3.12 is the newest allowed by the eval rules and the code needs >=3.9 for removesuffix and dict |). No reinstall step: test_cmd runs `$PY -c` with cwd = the repo copy, so sys.path[0] is the copy and `import llmcord` loads the working copy's file. The smoke command runs two checks and prints a pytest-style `N passed[, M failed] in Xs` line (verified with verify.parse_counts) and exits 1 on any failure: (1) compileall.compile_dir('.') over every .py file in the copy (excluding dot-dirs and node_modules), so a syntax error in llmcord.py or in any new module a migration adds fails; (2) importlib.import_module('llmcord') -- the only production module with an LLM call (llmcord.py:280 chat.completions.create) -- which executes all module-level code: the openai/discord/httpx/yaml/dotenv imports, load_dotenv(), get_config() reading ./config.yaml, discord Bot construction, slash-command and event registration, httpx.AsyncClient(). It then asserts on_message and main are callable and config['models'] is non-empty. The module ends with asyncio.run(main()), which would log in to Discord, so the check replaces asyncio.run with a stub that closes the coroutine before importing; nothing contacts Discord or an LLM. The AsyncOpenAI client is built per message inside on_message, so the LLM call path itself is not executed (no fake Discord message); the smoke only proves the code compiles and imports. Dummy env vars: OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-dummy, DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN=dummy-token, DISCORD_CLIENT_ID=0 (set in test_cmd and test_env); RAMP_ROUTER_API_KEY stays unset. HOME/TMPDIR are sandboxed into $ENV/home and $ENV/tmp, and PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=$ENV/tmp/pycache keeps compileall/import .pyc files out of the repo copy (no __pycache__ left in base). Negative checks on a scratch copy: renaming the openai import gives `1 passed, 1 failed`; a syntax error gives `0 passed, 2 failed`. discord.py logs two harmless WARNING lines (PyNaCl/davey not installed, voice unsupported). Baseline taken with outbound network denied (macOS sandbox-exec, loopback allowed) and RAMP_ROUTER_API_KEY unset: run 1 `2 passed in 1.36s` (1.6s wall), run 2 `2 passed in 0.77s` (1.0s wall); identical counts. Nothing deselected.
